title: EI and Cross Section
tagline: Cut the ski's layup at stations and compute, at each, the bending stiffness EI, torsional stiffness GJ, neutral axis and mass -- then the ski's flex numbers and weight.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: A ski's flex comes from its layup: every ply's shape and material. EI and Cross Section reads the layup straight from CAD (one solid per ply, each with an Onshape material), looks up the moduli in a CSV table, and gives EI(x), GJ(x), the neutral axis and the flex numbers -- so a design change shows its stiffness effect at once.
useWhen: You change a layup, core profile or sidecut
You need the EI curve for deflection, baseline or profile work
You compare a design with measured stiffness
slides.caption: ROY_Test: the output curves (EI, GJ ...) above the ski; the info reports repaired outlines.

points.head: FCP to ACP
points.body: N stations evenly spaced, one exactly at each contact point (numbered 0 ... N-1).

points.head: Tip and tail
points.body: Up to 4 extra each at about the same spacing; the tip's are numbered negative.

points.head: One cut per body
points.body: Outlines are cleaned (duplicates, micron gaps), triangulated and integrated.

points.head: Each body is a ply
points.body: Area, centroid height above the base, its own I, and its modulus E along the ski.

points.head: Neutral axis
points.body: The E-weighted centroid; EI is the stiffness about it.

points.head: E, not Q11
points.body: A narrow ski bends like a beam: Q11 would overstate by ~12 % (wood, Titanal), more for +-45 fabric.

slides.title: Example: ROY_Test, 35 stations
slides.head: EI peaks at 390 N m^2 under the foot; GJ follows (453); the neutral axis sits near mid-thickness
slides.body: Summary: 20.7 lb/in and 81.3 mm under 30 kg (variable EI); 16.2 lb/in prismatic. The stations cut 4 bodies with micron gaps, repaired (info).

points.head: The test
points.body: Simply supported at FCP and ACP, a point load at the mount (MRS).

points.head: Prismatic
points.body: P L^3 / (48 EI_avg): the average EI over the span.

points.head: Variable EI (Mohr)
points.body: P x integral s^2 / EI: the stiff middle counts more -- 20.7 vs 16.2 lb/in on ROY_Test.

items.head: Name materials exactly
items.body: The Onshape material name must match the CSV Name, case and spaces included; otherwise the body is ignored or needs data.

items.head: Turn off Create composites
items.body: It is the slowest step and only draws the section wires.

items.head: Wood cores
items.body: Some CSV rows (Aspen, Poplar) are isotropic placeholders: EI is fine, their GJ is overstated.

items.head: Ends
items.body: Planes grazing the tip or tail can lose a thin outline (console only).
